summary: This manuscript reports a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution artifacts show retrieval-augmentation was disabled, a single sampled candidate was reused per task across both arms, the deterministic validator judged all 250 sampled candidates valid (no repairs applied), and the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (McNemar two-sided p=1.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]). The paper transparently documents the preregistration deviation (RAG not exercised) and discusses limitations and next steps.
critical_issues: The archived analysis_results metadata (deviations_from_preregistration = []) contradicts the manuscript narrative that retrieval_augmented_generation was disabled; this inconsistency in the archived analysis/manifest must be reconciled and explicitly recorded (artifact-backed) so the preregistration deviation is machine-visible and traceable.

References and bibliography must be provided in a conventional IEEE numbered format with full bibliographic metadata (not bare DOIs/arXiv/identifier-only entries) so each numbered citation in prose is verifiable against a standard IEEE-style References section.

The Methods must explicitly and unambiguously state the runtime sampling semantics: confirm that exactly one sampled initial generation call per task was used and reused by both arms (shared_initial_candidate), and reiterate that model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset which does not imply temperature=0; this explicit sentence must appear in Methods to avoid misinterpretation.
required_revisions: Update archived analysis_results and/or execution_manifest to include an explicit deviations_from_preregistration entry documenting that retrieval_augmented_generation was disabled (point to model_configuration.json and execution manifest hashes), or (if the archived metadata is immutable) add a short explicit machine-verifiable Deviations subsection in Methods/Results that references the exact artifact paths and hashes demonstrating the deviation.

Replace or confirm the References section as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full metadata for each cited record; ensure all inline citations use numeric IEEE markers and that each cited record supports the proximate claim (adjust wording if a cited source only proposes rather than empirically demonstrates a claim).

Add a concise explicit sentence in Methods stating: (a) exactly one initial sample per task was taken and reused across baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), and (b) temperature=null/unset in model_configuration.json does not imply deterministic sampling (temperature=0). Reference the model_configuration.json artifact hash in the manuscript text.
optional_revisions: Add brief analysis or discussion hypothesizing why the validator accepted all sampled candidates (e.g., task-generator / model alignment, task difficulty, or distributional proximity) and, where possible, link to representative task examples in the archived bundle to aid readers' interpretation.

Add a short note in Discussion suggesting concrete follow-up preregistration edits (enable retrieval_augmented_generation, controlled-poison corpus with provenance flags, and independent per-condition sampling) and point readers to the exact artifacts that would be produced by such a follow-up run to facilitate reproducibility.
